subject: DPA & Data-retention carve-outs for backup/DR — Acme Logistics
messages:
From: Claire Dunne <claire.dunne@acme-logistics.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-logistics.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme-logistics.com>
Date: 2025-08-03T14:22:00Z
Subject: DPA & retention specifics for Acme — initial ask

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Legal had a few follow-ups on the DPA — primarily around data retention and backups. Two specific asks: (1) confirm Redwood's position on deletion vs. de-identification for customer data (Acme wants guarantees that data is deleted within X days on contract termination), and (2) we need clarity on backups/DR: Acme insists on a carve-out that allows Redwood to retain encrypted snapshots for 90 days for DR purposes but wants a guarantee those backups won't be used for any product training or analytics.

Can you share an editable redline or let us know who from your legal team we should loop in? We also need your subprocessors list and any data transfer mechanisms you rely on for EU->US transfers (SCCs, etc.).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement window is tight.

Thanks,
Claire
Procurement Manager, Acme Logistics

Attachments: none
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
To: Claire Dunne <claire.dunne@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-08-03T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA & retention specifics for Acme — initial ask

Hi Claire,

Thanks — looping in Rishi (Legal) and Lauren (Security/Compliance). High-level answers up front:
- Deletion: Redwood commits to customer-directed deletion of customer content and associated metadata within 30 days of termination; backups are a special case (see below).
- Backups/DR carve-out: We permit encrypted disaster recovery snapshots to be retained for up to 90 days after deletion triggers strictly for restore purposes only; they are excluded from training/analytics and access is highly restricted.
- Subprocessors & transfers: attaching our current subprocessor list and SOC 2 summary; we rely on EU SCCs for EU->US transfers and provide exporter/importer details upon request.

I attached a starting redline of the DPA with the proposed language for the backup carve-out and a separate Backup Access Controls addendum. Rishi — can you review the redline and confirm acceptable guardrails for Acme's ask? Lauren — can you confirm the technical controls (encryption at rest, split-key for backups, access auditability)?

Next steps: Rishi to propose legal language; if Acme is OK with the redline we can send via DocuSign.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success (contracts liaison)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Redline_Acme_20250803.pdf, SOC2-Report-Redwood-2024.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, Claire Dunne <claire.dunne@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-08-04T09:13:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA & retention specifics for Acme — proposed redlines

Claire / Neha,

Attached is a focused legal redline (see pdf) that inserts the following buckets:
1) Termination deletion: Redwood will delete customer content and metadata within 30 days after contract termination or written request, except where retention is required by law.
2) Backup/DR carve-out: Encrypted backups used solely for disaster recovery may be retained for a maximum of 90 days post-deletion; such backups will not be used for model training, feature-development, telemetry, or analytics and access will be limited to a named small ops group under documented emergency-only procedures.
3) Subprocessors: we list current subprocessors and commit to notice of material changes; customers with specific objections can request additional controls or an assessment.
4) Data transfers: we will rely on SCCs for transfers from the EU and maintain Transparency Logs on transfer locations.

Claire — two clarifying Qs that will affect language: (a) is Acme comfortable with a 30-day deletion window for primary data and 90 days for backups, or are they asking for shorter windows; (b) do you require backups be subject to the same deletion upon request (i.e., immediate purge of backup copies) or is the 90-day carve-out acceptable?

If Acme needs immediate removal of backups, we can propose an accommodated SLA that includes an emergency purge service (additional fee + lead time for some cloud providers).

Rishi Malhotra
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Redline_Acme_20250804.pdf
From: Claire Dunne <claire.dunne@acme-logistics.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-logistics.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, Acme Legal <legal@acme-logistics.com>
Date: 2025-08-05T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA & retention specifics for Acme — proposed redlines

Rishi — thanks for the quick turn.

Acme's position: we need a guaranteed deletion of primary data within 30 days; for backups, the 90-day DR carve-out is acceptable only if we get these assurances:
- backups are encrypted with customer-unique keys or a split-key approach so Redwood cannot unilaterally decrypt them for any other purpose;
- a sworn statement that backups will not be used for training/analytics and a contractual audit right to verify;
- an explicit exception that legal holds (e.g., subpoenas) will extend retention but Acme must be notified promptly.

If Redwood can accept the three items above in the DPA, we can proceed to signature. Assuming that, please send the final DPA via DocuSign and include the signed SOC2 as a referenced exhibit.

Best,
Claire

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redlines_annotated.pdf
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
To: Claire Dunne <claire.dunne@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-08-06T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA & retention specifics for Acme — final DPA & DocuSign

Claire — appreciate the clarity. Per your three bullet points, we have:
- Keying: we will maintain customer-specific encryption keys for backup snapshots where supported by the target cloud; where split-key is required we will document options and operational constraints in an exhibit.
- Use restriction & audit: DPA now includes explicit prohibition on backup use for training/analytics and a contractual right to audit (reasonable notice + confidentiality protections).
- Legal hold: DPA contains language that legal obligations can extend retention and Redwood will provide prompt notice and limited details as permitted by law.

I've attached the updated fully-executed DPA draft and initiated a DocuSign envelope (link below). Also attached is the SOC2 report as requested. Please route to your signatory; once we see the signed envelope we'll provision the account with the backup keying options you selected.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ACME-98765
Attachments: DocuSign-Envelope-ACME-98765.pdf, SOC2-Report-Redwood-2024.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if any technical detail on the backup keying approach would help.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-logistics.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, Claire Dunne <claire.dunne@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-logistics.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
Date: 2025-08-07T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA & retention specifics for Acme — signed

Neha / team — signed and returned via DocuSign this morning. Appreciate the responsiveness here; we'll confirm the keying option (customer-managed vs. Redwood-managed split-key) in the onboarding form but happy to proceed.

Tom Rivers
Head of IT Operations, Acme Logistics
